title: AlignSurvey: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Human Preferences Alignment in Social Surveys

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model-predicted survey responses and attitude stances against ground-truth human distributions across different income, education, and occupation subgroups using Wasserstein Distance and classification accuracy, highlighting representational disparities for low-income and manual labor populations.

Analyzing the alignment of LLM-generated survey responses and qualitative opinions with actual human survey data across various age brackets, specifically measuring the accuracy gap and representational fidelity for elderly populations (e.g., 76+ years).
Assessing the fidelity of model responses conditioned on urban versus rural demographic profiles by comparing predicted attitude distributions to real-world national survey data.

Measuring the accuracy, F1-score, and distribution alignment (Wasserstein Distance) of structured survey responses and attitude stances generated by LLMs when conditioned on male versus female demographic profiles.
